phases.title: Your regular party
phases.summary: A balanced setup for ordinary encounters. On battle days, this panel changes where the matchup calls for a different party.

members.name: Protagonist
members.role: Back row. Use magic for weaknesses; save the stronger spells for enemies that need them.
members.inherit: One cheap Mage spell: Bot (Mage 1), Blizz (Mage 2) or Kande (Mage 6). Each costs 4 MP. Choose the element needed for the outing.
members.requires: Your Mage 20 and Gallica bond 3, then study Wizard.
members.fallback: Keep Mage. Its cheap spells remain useful. Extra A-EXP on a mastered Archetype earns Hero’s Leaf of Light items for training another studied Archetype.
members.train: Wizard 11 for Shield Blessing. While a stat buff is active, it restores MP during battle. Hulkenberg can supply Rakukaja from Magic Knight rank 1.

members.name: Strohl
members.role: Front row when attacking. Use its group attacks when they save actions; ordinary sword attacks cost no MP.
members.inherit: Diagonal Slash (Warrior 1, 5 MP) for a cheap single-target skill. Use Slicer (Warrior 8, 12 MP) instead when more damage is worth the cost.
members.requires: Warrior rank 20 on Strohl and Strohl bond 3.
members.fallback: Mastered Warrior is still a good single-target option and keeps its own damage passives.
members.train: Continue Swordmaster toward 20. Avoid buying every expensive inherited passive at once.

members.name: Hulkenberg
members.role: Healing and defence, with ordinary lance attacks when she has a safe opening. Stay back while healing.
members.inherit: Medi (her Healer 3, 10 MP). If her Cleric is rank 3, Medica is the stronger 20-MP alternative. Equip one reliable party heal first.
members.requires: Knight 20 and Mage 10 on Hulkenberg, plus Hulkenberg bond 3. Mastering Knight alone is not enough.
members.fallback: Knight with the same inherited heal. Do not switch to an untrained Mage for a hard fight just to meet the upgrade requirement.
members.train: Mage 10 if missing; then Magic Knight. Cleric 3 is a useful short detour for Medica if she has not learned it.

members.name: Heismay
members.role: Dark damage, items and support. Lurking Nightblade also lowers the target’s Hit/Evasion, but costs 16 MP.
members.inherit: Plunder Magic (his Thief 11) to recover his own MP. It costs 1 MP; the amount stolen varies. With a spare slot, Mudo (Thief 4, 4 MP) gives a cheaper Dark attack.
members.requires: His Thief 20 and Heismay bond 3, then study Assassin.
members.fallback: Keep mastered Thief for its cheap Mudo and native Plunder Magic. You do not lose training progress by staying on it.
members.train: Gunner 3 is a useful small investment for Poison Shot and ranged Pierce attacks. Then continue Assassin.

notes: Keep your usual setup on town days. Follower conversations do not require a matching Archetype.
Each character must learn a skill personally before inheriting it. An upgrade has its own skill list; earlier skills do not automatically carry across.
Buy the listed inheritance in Akademeia and equip it in the Archetype menu. After changing classes, equip a suitable current weapon; a starter weapon can make the new class feel much weaker.
For ordinary fights, ambush first and use free attacks when they will finish the enemy. Use healing items between fights when that saves MP; a party heal is unnecessary for one small injury.

Bronze III: use the protagonist as Seeker, Strohl as Swordmaster, Hulkenberg as Magic Knight or Knight with inherited Medi/Medica, and Heismay as Faker. Keep Mage and Healer forms out of the active party. Use group physical damage, then remove the remaining enemy’s evasion buff with Dekaja (Faker 13); Sukunda (Faker 5) is a fallback if learned.
Bronze II is field combat: put the protagonist on Mage/Wizard or Seeker. The squad-battle setup is not the focus of this match.

An inherited Poison Shot (Gunner 3) supplies Pierce from the back row for the other target. Allies and Synthesis cannot help.

Silver III: restore all four party members and bring single-target Fire, Ice, physical damage and a party heal. Hit Azure with Fire, Ochre with Ice and Platinum with physical attacks. Avoid all-target elemental spells while Platinum remains. Gold Attack (Merchant 1, 500 reeve) supplies Almighty for Golden; without it, finish the others first and use physical damage while keeping the party healed.

Silver II: this is field combat with a 90-second limit. Put the protagonist on Seeker for its support-attack passive, equip a current sword and dodge the large enemies before attacking again. Your squad spells are not the main tool in this match.

Silver I: take only the protagonist and Hulkenberg, both on Brawler or a trained Pugilist. Inherit Hamaon (Cleric 1), or Hama (Healer 1), on the protagonist. Give Hulkenberg Medica (Cleric 3), or Medi (Healer 3). Use Light on the Fighter first, then Strike on the Mage. Protect Ice weaknesses if you have suitable equipment; carry Daze cures and keep HP high because Brawler attacks spend HP. Brawler needs Catherina 1 and each character’s own study; Pugilist is optional. Prioritise the protagonist’s Light spell and Hulkenberg’s heal if each has only one inheritance slot.

Gold III: only the protagonist fights. Equip Prince and inherit Blizza (Wizard 2). Use Ice while the target has no magic-reflect barrier. After Mage Mirror appears, stop casting elemental spells: move to the front row and use Heroic Slash or, at Prince 20, Royal Slash. Royal Sword is a Synthesis skill and cannot be used alone. Carry healing and a buff-removing item if available; your allies cannot act.

Gold II: the protagonist fights in the field and must avoid every hit. Use Prince, or Gunner with a current crossbow for ranged attacks. Dodge first, then take a short attack opening. Party healing cannot rescue a failed no-hit attempt.

Gold I: the opponent resists ordinary damage types. Use Prince’s Royal Sword Synthesis with an ally, or Royal Slash once Prince reaches 20. Keep healing and revival ready; repeated ordinary elemental spells are inefficient.

Championship: use the four-person cards with Ice/Pierce coverage and win within two rounds. The protagonist and Junah can use Blizza; Strohl can inherit Icy Strike (General 2), and Hulkenberg can replace Dekunda with Heavy Rush (Magic Knight 9). Keep useful attacks ahead of unnecessary buffing. Hero’s Cry needs Prince 13 and 99 MP. Check Synthesis and accessory costs before entering; use the pre-entry save if your damage is insufficient.

Gold Gauntlet: enter only when the receptionist offers Gold: The Furthest Reaches. Restore all four equipped party members and start with healing, revival and enough resources for 30 consecutive fights. Check affinities and use cheap effective attacks. This endurance event is separate from the ranked ladder and Champion Battle.

Keep Mage and Healer forms out of the active party. Use group physical damage, then remove the remaining enemy’s evasion buff with Dekaja (Faker 13); Sukunda (Faker 5) is a fallback if learned.
Bronze II is field combat: put the protagonist on Mage/Wizard or Seeker. The squad-battle setup is not the focus of this match.

Bronze I is solo: use Magic Seeker if the protagonist has Seeker 20 and More bond 3, otherwise Seeker. Defeat the Wind-weak target first. Bring his own healing and Forget/Hex/Poison cures. An inherited Poison Shot (Gunner 3) supplies Pierce from the back row for the other target. Allies and Synthesis cannot help.

Silver III: restore all four party members and bring single-target Fire, Ice, physical damage and a party heal. Hit Azure with Fire, Ochre with Ice and Platinum with physical attacks. Avoid all-target elemental spells while Platinum remains. Gold Attack (Merchant 1, 500 reeve) supplies Almighty for Golden; without it, finish the others first and use physical damage while keeping the party healed.

Silver II: this is field combat with a 90-second limit. Put the protagonist on Seeker for its support-attack passive, equip a current sword and dodge the large enemies before attacking again. Your squad spells are not the main tool in this match.

Silver I: take only the protagonist and Hulkenberg, both on Brawler or a trained Pugilist. Inherit Hamaon (Cleric 1), or Hama (Healer 1), on the protagonist. Give Hulkenberg Medica (Cleric 3), or Medi (Healer 3). Use Light on the Fighter first, then Strike on the Mage. Protect Ice weaknesses if you have suitable equipment; carry Daze cures and keep HP high because Brawler attacks spend HP. Brawler needs Catherina 1 and each character’s own study; Pugilist is optional. Prioritise the protagonist’s Light spell and Hulkenberg’s heal if each has only one inheritance slot.

Gold III: only the protagonist fights. Equip Prince and inherit Blizza (Wizard 2). Use Ice while the target has no magic-reflect barrier. After Mage Mirror appears, stop casting elemental spells: move to the front row and use Heroic Slash or, at Prince 20, Royal Slash. Royal Sword is a Synthesis skill and cannot be used alone. Carry healing and a buff-removing item if available; your allies cannot act.

Gold II: the protagonist fights in the field and must avoid every hit. Use Prince, or Gunner with a current crossbow for ranged attacks. Dodge first, then take a short attack opening. Party healing cannot rescue a failed no-hit attempt.

Gold I: the opponent resists ordinary damage types. Use Prince’s Royal Sword Synthesis with an ally, or Royal Slash once Prince reaches 20. Keep healing and revival ready; repeated ordinary elemental spells are inefficient.

Championship: use the four-person cards with Ice/Pierce coverage and win within two rounds. The protagonist and Junah can use Blizza; Strohl can inherit Icy Strike (General 2), and Hulkenberg can replace Dekunda with Heavy Rush (Magic Knight 9). Keep useful attacks ahead of unnecessary buffing. Hero’s Cry needs Prince 13 and 99 MP. Check Synthesis and accessory costs before entering; use the pre-entry save if your damage is insufficient.

Gold Gauntlet: enter only when the receptionist offers Gold: The Furthest Reaches. Restore all four equipped party members and start with healing, revival and enough resources for 30 consecutive fights. Check affinities and use cheap effective attacks. This endurance event is separate from the ranked ladder and Champion Battle.

day-october-26.title: Final outing party
day-october-26.summary: Take a developed party with full resources. Keep the guide’s separate trophy-route instructions in view.

members.name: Protagonist
members.role: Main damage and flexible Synthesis support. Keep your Magic build: Royal Sword uses the higher of Strength or Magic.
members.inherit: Shield Blessing (Wizard 11), then Blizza (Wizard 2): two slots. Shield Blessing needs an active Attack, Defence or Hit/Evasion buff. Use Blizza for an Ice weakness instead of spending on a large Synthesis attack.
members.requires: Automatically obtained during the completed September story. Each inherited skill must first be learned by the protagonist and purchased in Skill Inheritance.
members.fallback: Wizard remains a good exploration choice. Elemental Master is available with Gallica 8 and Wizard 20; keep the cheaper inherited spells for small enemies.
members.train: Ongoing training goals: Prince 9 for field HP/MP recovery through allies’ support attacks, 13 for Hero’s Cry and 20 for Royal Slash. You do not need all three today; use the skills you have actually learned.

members.name: Strohl
members.role: Physical attacker and backup party buffer. Use the cheapest attack that finishes an enemy; large attacks are for durable targets.
members.inherit: Slash Boost (Warrior 20) and Marakukaja (Commander 1): two slots. Marakukaja raises the whole party’s Defence.
members.requires: Strohl bond 7, Swordmaster 20 and General 10 on Strohl. General itself needs Bardon 3 and Commander 20.
members.fallback: Keep Swordmaster if Samurai is locked. Prioritise the defence buff over a damage passive if you have only one free slot.
members.train: Optional Royal Warrior: Strohl bond 8, Samurai 20 and Warlord 20. Warlord needs Bardon 8 and General 20. Do not delay the route to force this upgrade.

members.name: Hulkenberg
members.archetype: Paladin if ready; otherwise Magic Knight
members.role: Durable healer and defender. Heal first when the party is hurt; drawing attacks is a separate action and cannot also heal the party.
members.inherit: Medica (Cleric 3) and Dekunda (Healer 13): two slots. Medica heals everyone; Dekunda clears the party’s stat reductions.
members.requires: Hulkenberg bond 7 and Magic Knight 20. Medica must be learned on Hulkenberg herself. Cleric needs Maria 3 and Healer 20.
members.fallback: Magic Knight with inherited Medica and Dekunda. If Medica is unlearned, Mediline (Magic Knight 5, 10 MP) heals allies in her row; move anyone needing it into that row before she casts.
members.train: Ongoing upgrade goals: Paladin 20 for Revitalise 3 and MP recovery. Optional Royal Knight needs bond 8, Paladin 20, Dark Knight 15 and Elemental Master 15. Keep the listed fallback while training; these are not all required today.

members.name: Junah
members.archetype: Persona Master if ready; otherwise Masked Dancer · Wizard’s Mask
members.role: Debuffs and economical elemental coverage. The mask provides Blizza, Kandera and Shield Blessing; it occupies her accessory slot.
members.inherit: Tarunda (Faker 3) and Dekaja (Faker 13): two slots. Lower a dangerous enemy’s Attack; remove its buffs when they appear.
members.requires: Junah bond 6, Masked Dancer 20 and Faker 10. Make Wizard’s Mask in Akademeia with a Magician White Mask and Priestess White Mask after Wizard is unlocked.
members.fallback: Masked Dancer with the same mask and inherited skills. Without that mask, use an available elemental mask and let the protagonist handle Ice. If Dekaja is unlearned, bring an item that removes enemy buffs.
members.train: Ongoing goal: Faker 13 for Dekaja. Optional Royal Masked Dancer also needs Junah 8, Persona Master 20 and Trickster 20. Use the listed current setup or fallback today; there is no need to complete all this training first.

notes: Prince remains suitable for your Magic build. Use trained Royal upgrades if you have them; otherwise keep the listed Samurai, Paladin and Persona Master roles.

Give the healer your strongest suitable party heal. If Hulkenberg has Saviour 3, inherit Medicall instead of Medica for heavier recovery; it costs 40 MP. Keep revival and ailment cures available on other characters too.
Prepare for a long battle with frequent party-wide damage and stat reductions. Do not spend all MP in the first stretch; use the recovery items you have saved.
Use Dekaja and Dekunda when needed. Do not mistake repeatedly rebuilding maximum buffs for making progress if the enemy keeps removing them.

Keep reserve characters equipped and ready. If the current team cannot survive the full-strength encounter, use the permanent pre-finale save for more preparation instead of weakening the trophy target.
